propositions: Three CLI verb-names are being renamed under a new bridge noun: bridge-fsck→bridge fsck, bridge-probe→bridge check-access, jira-onboard→bridge setup.
All three old spellings remain functional as compatibility entrypoints that route to identical implementations preserving parser behavior, output schemas, and exit codes.
The bridge setup verb accepts entrypoint-specific argparse prog parameter, calling check-access as its final validation step with environment overlay support and --no-validate escape hatch.

Every consumer site—CLI dispatch, help text, schema IDs, tests, scripts, CI workflows, and documentation—must be migrated to canonical noun-based spellings with old spellings explicitly preserved in compatibility/history/test sections.
check-access is registered as a primary verb sibling to fsck under the bridge subparser group (not a flag), because it creates and deletes real Jira issues unlike read-only flag precedents.
Behavioral parity tests prove both spellings succeed, fail identically, and produce matching output/exit status across options, arguments, and representative failure modes.
